'''Robert Joseph Cava''' {{post-nominals|ForMemRS}} (born 1951)<ref name=gdansk>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531152619/http://pg.edu.pl/documents/10607/2601239/Cava_en.pdf|archive-date=2016-05-31|url=http://pg.edu.pl/documents/10607/2601239/Cava_en.pdf|title=Robert J. Cava (born 1951)|publisher=pg.edu.pl|location=Gdansk}}</ref> is a solid-state chemist at [[Princeton University]] where he holds the title [[Princeton University Department of Chemistry|Russell Wellman Moore Professor of Chemistry]].<ref>[https://www.princeton.edu/~cavalab/group/bossResume.html CV in Princeton]</ref> Previously, Professor Cava worked as a staff scientist at [[Bell labs]] from 1979–1996, where earned the title of Distinguished Member of the Technical Staff. {{As of|2016}} his research investigates [[topological insulators]], [[semimetal]]s, [[superconductor]]s, [[Geometrical frustration|frustrated magnets]] and [[thermoelectric effect|thermoelectrics]].<ref name=cavalab>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501122015/http://chemists.princeton.edu/cava/|archive-date=2016-05-01|url=http://chemists.princeton.edu/cava/|publisher=princeton.edu|location=[[Princeton, New Jersey]]|title=Cava Laboratory: Solid State Chemistry Research Group}}</ref><ref name=cv/><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref>[https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/47044 Oral history interview transcript for Robert Cava on 9 April 2021, American Institute of Physics, Niels Bohr Library & Archives]</ref>

==Education==
Cava was educated at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) where he was awarded [[Bachelor of Science]] and [[Master of Science]] degrees in [[Materials Science]] and [[Engineering]] in 1974 followed by a [[PhD]] in [[ceramic]]s in 1978.<ref name=cv/> His PhD was supervised by Bernhardt J. Wuensch<ref name=wuensch/> and investigated the [[electrical mobility]] of [[ion]]s in [[fast ion conductor]]s.<ref name=cavaphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Robert Joseph|last=Cava |title=A study of the mobile ions in several binary fast ion conductors |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=1978 |oclc= 5881992|id={{ProQuest|302912364}}}}</ref><ref name=CavaReidinger1977>{{cite journal|last1=Cava|first1=R.J.|last2=Reidinger|first2=F.|last3=Wuensch|first3=B.J.|title=Single-crystal neutron-diffraction study of AgI between 23° and 300°C|journal=Solid State Communications|volume=24|issue=6|year=1977|pages=411–416|doi=10.1016/0038-1098(77)91306-0|bibcode=1977SSCom..24..411C}}</ref><ref name=bjwuensch>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531124844/http://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=63006|archive-date=2016-05-31|url=http://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=63006|publisher=academictree.org|title=Bernhardt J. Wuensch: Chemistry Tree}}</ref>

==Career and research==
In his career, he has published over 500 peer-reviewed papers, 36 of them in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' and 8 of them in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=R.J. Cava |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=cUt3CuEAAAAJ&view_op=list_works |access-date=2023-06-08 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> These papers have been cited over 30,000 times,<ref name=":0" /> including his seminal work on Ba<sub>2</sub>YCu<sub>3</sub>O<sub>9−δ</sub> ([[Yttrium barium copper oxide|YBCO]]), which has been cited almost 1500 times.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Cava|first=Robert|title=Bulk superconductivity at 91 K in single-phase oxygen-deficient perovskite Ba2YCu3O9-δ|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|date=20 April 1987|volume=58|issue=16|pages=1676–1679|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.1676|pmid=10034505|display-authors=etal|bibcode=1987PhRvL..58.1676C|doi-access=free}}</ref> He holds 15 patents.{{citation needed|date=May 2016}}
[[File:Cava i Krawczyk2.jpg|thumbnail|right|Professor Robert J. Cava during the ceremony of receiving the Doctor Honoris Causa degree from the [[Gdańsk University of Technology]]]] His former doctoral students include [[Leslie Schoop]].<ref name=sphd/>

===Honors and awards===
In recognition of his contributions, he was elected in 1988 a fellow of the [[American Institute of Physics]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?cavar |title=Robert Cava |work=Array of Contemporary American Physicists |publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]] |access-date=16 September 2012 |archive-date=8 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808221350/http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?cavar |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1988&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date= 26 September 2020}}</ref> He was elected in 2001 a [[Member of the National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321155955/http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/14980.html|archive-date=2016-03-21|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/robert-j-cava-e27pvs/ |title=Cava, Robert J. |work=Member Directory |publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]] |url-status=live|access-date=16 September 2012 }}</ref> who specifically acknowledged his mastery of the ternary and quaternary oxides that produced materials possessing [[high-temperature superconductivity]].

In 1996 Cava received the [[Bernd T. Matthias Prize]] for new superconducting materials.  He received in 2011 the [[Humboldt Prize]] and in 2012 the [[Linus Pauling Award]]. In 2014 he received a Doctor Honoris Causa degree from the [[Gdańsk University of Technology]]. Cava also won the 2021 [[David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Cava&first_nm=Robert&year=2021|title = Prize Recipient}}</ref> In addition to research, Cava's ability to connect with students while teaching has earned him several teaching awards, including the Fall 2002 Excellence in Teaching Award from [[Princeton University]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531145744/http://chemists.princeton.edu/cava/files/2014/04/Cava_CV_2014.pdf|archive-date=2016-05-31|url=http://chemists.princeton.edu/cava/files/2014/04/Cava_CV_2014.pdf|title=Robert J. Cava CV: Russell Wellman Moore Professor of Chemistry|publisher=princeton.edu|location=[[Princeton, New Jersey]]}}</ref>

[[File:Cava i Krawczyk.jpg|thumbnail|Professor Robert J. Cava and rector of the [[Gdańsk University of Technology]], Professor Henryk Krawczyk, during the ceremony of receiving the Doctor Honoris Causa degree]]

He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2016|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS) in 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/robert-cava-12850/|title=Professor Robert Cava ForMemRS|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160429121105/https://royalsociety.org/people/robert-cava-12850/|archive-date=2016-04-29}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=September 25, 2015 }}}}</ref> 

==Personal life==
His biography at the [[Gdańsk University of Technology]] describes him as a [[New York City|New Yorker]], dedicated supporter of the [[New York Yankees]], passionate astronomer and [[Homebrewing|amateur brewer]].<ref name=gdansk/>
